title: Wittmann wins at home after Juncadella takes pole at the Norisring
dek: Marco Wittmann climbed from seventh on the grid to win Race 2 at the Norisring for BMW Team RMG by 0.450 seconds from Edoardo Mortara, with pole-sitter Daniel Juncadella third.

chapters.title: Saturday’s winner, and a lead changes hands
text: Saturday’s race had gone to Edoardo Mortara, who converted pole into victory for Mercedes-AMG ahead of team-mate Gary Paffett and Marco Wittmann, the local BMW driver standing on the Norisring podium for the first time. Paffett’s second place lifted him to 97 points and the championship lead, six clear of Timo Glock on 91.

Audi left Saturday with no points at all, its best finisher Jamie Green in eleventh, so Sunday’s second race offered the Ingolstadt marque a chance to recover while the title contenders looked for a way to stay close to Paffett.

chapters.title: Juncadella beats Paffett by 0.034 seconds
text: Audi enjoyed a brighter start to Sunday’s session, with Nico Müller, Loïc Duval and Robin Frijns each going to the top of the order in the early minutes. Mercedes-AMG soon took control: Paffett was the first driver below 48 seconds and ended the first half of qualifying at the top on 47.739, ahead of Mortara, di Resta and the best BMW, Wittmann.

Di Resta and Lucas Auer got close to Paffett with two minutes left, but it was Daniel Juncadella who lowered the best time, to 47.705, just as the session was red-flagged because Frijns had stopped in the escape road at the Turn 1 hairpin. One minute was added, giving the drivers time for two more flying laps, but nobody in the top ten improved and Juncadella held pole.

Paffett was second, 0.034 seconds behind, with Auer (47.834), di Resta (47.882) and Mortara (47.886), who touched the wall on his last lap, completing an all-Mercedes top five. Bruno Spengler led the BMWs in sixth, 0.006 seconds ahead of Wittmann, with Joel Eriksson, Glock and Philipp Eng in eighth, ninth and tenth. Müller was 11th and best of the Audis, and Pascal Wehrlein’s Mercedes was last of the 18 cars.

chapters.title: Mortara stops first and Wittmann starts to climb
text: Juncadella held the lead at the start, with Auer getting ahead of Paffett into second. Mortara, Eriksson, Müller, Rockenfeller and Green all took their mandatory stops with a tyre change at the end of the first lap, Mortara coming in from fifth place. That made the early running a game of positions, with the rest of the field waiting for a window.

Wittmann, from seventh, had quickly closed up on di Resta and could not find a way past until di Resta stopped early from fourth. That released the BMW into clear air, and Wittmann made his own stop around lap ten to twelve. He rejoined in the midfield, used Spengler’s car to his advantage in a convoy, and squeezed past the Team RBM car to put several places between himself and Mortara.

chapters.title: Fresh tyres decide it for Wittmann
text: Once the stops had worked through, Wittmann had the best tyres of the leaders. On around lap 22 he and Juncadella fought hard for the lead, Wittmann first having to yield the place to the Spaniard before taking the front a lap later, his first kilometres at the head of the field in a home race. In the lead on the road he could pull clear of the Mercedes pair.

Behind them the battle for the championship played out. Paffett, who had stopped on lap 11, was slow to rejoin and lost three places to di Resta, Müller and Glock on cold tyres, and the two title rivals ran together for roughly 20 laps. The Mercedes was faster on the straights, the BMW better in the tight corners. Paffett ran into the back of Glock at the hairpin after a lock-up and later lost two places in a slide, ending the fight, and he said afterwards that Glock’s defence was unfair. Glock held tenth, the last points position, and Paffett finished 13th, out of the points.

chapters.title: Mortara closes, Wittmann holds on by 0.450 seconds
text: Wittmann built a lead of around 2.5 seconds with a quarter of the race remaining, but as the laps ran down Mortara, whose early stop on lap one had left him on a long final tyre stint, cut the gap steadily. The Mercedes was faster at the end than the BMW, but Wittmann said he pushed to the limit and just had enough; he crossed the line 0.450 seconds ahead after 68 laps.

Juncadella was 0.860 seconds behind in third, with Spengler fourth, 5.497 seconds back, ahead of Auer and di Resta. Müller was seventh and Frijns eighth, the best Audis, with Frijns having made up places from 16th on the grid with a first stint lasting until lap 40, and Wehrlein ninth after a similarly long opening stint. Glock took the final point in tenth. Rast, the defending champion, lost time in a pit stop with a problem at the left rear wheel and finished 14th, one place ahead of Green.

chapters.title: Mortara joins the title fight
text: Wittmann called it the race of his life and said it felt almost like winning a championship, having tried to win at home for years without even making the podium. After Saturday’s third place he had joked that he would skip second and go straight for first, and he delivered it from seventh on the grid, without a safety car or any drama to help him. It was his first home win at the Norisring and his second win of the season, after the Hungaroring. He added that the Mercedes had been a little quicker than him at the end.

Mortara, who completed a weekend of first and second, said he had made the stop on the first lap, which was bad for his tyres, but that the car was much better than on Saturday and he gave everything for the win. Juncadella was pleased with his podium and described the difficult moment after his stop that allowed Wittmann through, adding that the tyres took about five laps to warm up. Mercedes-AMG’s team principal Ulrich Fritz called it an incredible finish and said the team had had a very successful weekend.

Paffett called the fight with Glock a disaster and was openly angry about it, comparing it unfavourably with their race at Hockenheim, but he left Nuremberg still leading the standings. After the double-header he had 99 points, Mortara moved up to second on 93, six behind, and Wittmann and Glock shared third on 92.

For Audi, Dieter Gass said the weekend had been better than Saturday, with two cars in the points. He regretted the pit-stop problem for Rast, whose car had the best pace of the Audis. Müller, the best Audi in seventh, said the team had picked up some important points and hoped to collect more at Zandvoort, where the series raced next, with Race 1 on 14 July.

facts.v: Wittmann won Race 2 from seventh on the grid, 0.450 seconds ahead of Mortara after 68 laps.

facts.v: Juncadella took pole with a 47.705 at the end of a red-flagged session, 0.034 seconds ahead of Paffett.

facts.t: Fastest pit stop of the weekend
facts.v: BMW Team RMG recorded a 38.591-second stop, the fastest of the Norisring weekend, and earned 25 points in the Hankook Best Pit Stop Award.
